title: Mode resolved self-organized circular polarization asymmetry in a nonchiral random fiber laser
task: Mode-resolved circular polarization asymmetry in nonchiral random fiber laser via modal interference
key_results: Positive and negative circular Stokes S₃/S₀ at selected spectral modes above lasing threshold (zero below); circular polarization emerges from interference of overlapping linearly polarized modes with different gains, not material chirality
comments: Novel insight that polarization is an emergent property of modal dynamics rather than a material fingerprint; two-mode non-Hermitian model provides good qualitative agreement, though quantitative fitting details absent.

model_io.model: Polymer optical fiber doped with laser dye + nonchiral scatterers (experiment)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Circular polarization in nonchiral random laser emerges from mode interference and gain competition, not material or structural chirality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; S₃/S₀ shows both handedness components near/above threshold; two-mode model explains emergence via spectral overlap and differential gain

title: Controlling intertwined electronic orders in FeSe with exfoliation
task: Controlling competing electronic orders (nematic vs. superconducting) in FeSe via exfoliation
key_results: Exfoliation suppresses bulk nematic response; switches superconducting symmetry from s-wave (bulk) to d-wave-dominant (thin flakes); confirmed by angle-dependent Andreev reflection spectroscopy
comments: Novel and elegant control mechanism; dimensional reduction as a 'chemical-free' tuning knob is appealing, though mechanism underlying symmetry switch (disorder, proximity, interface effects) remains to be clarified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dimensional reduction weakens nematic order and shifts superconducting pairing symmetry from s-wave to d-wave
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nematic response suppressed and Andreev spectra show transition from zero-energy bound states to coherence peaks with rotation angle

comments: Elegant solution to RF-power consumption and experimental complexity; divacancy-specific implementation in SiC is promising for scalable quantum platforms, though generalization to other color centers unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: MW-driven electron spin can coherently manipulate coupled nuclear spin through hyperfine interaction without RF fields when external magnetic field is precisely tilted
